chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Najran from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
I said to him, 'Should the one who washed the deceased perform ghusl?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And the one who places him in the grave?' He said, 'No, for he only touches the clothes.'
ai.seo_question: Who is required to perform ghusl after handling a deceased body according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the distinction between major ritual impurity (janabah) requiring full ghusl and minor contact that does not necessitate it, specifically contrasting the washer of the deceased with the one who buries them. Scholarly commentary notes that while washing involves direct contact with the body's moisture and pores, the burier typically handles only the shroud, thus remaining in a state of lesser impurity. This ruling underscores the practical jurisprudence of handling death rituals in Shia fiqh, emphasizing the physical nature of ritual purity over mere proximity.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Should he wash, the one who washed the deceased?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘The one who enters into his grave?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but rather, he would touch the clothes (of the deceased)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn abu Najran from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if one who gives Ghusl (bath) to a dead person is required to take Ghusl (bath). He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he is required to take Ghusl (bath).’ I then asked if one who places the deceased in the grave is required to take Ghusl (bath). He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he is not required to take Ghusl (bath) because he only touches the cloth.’”
